cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg32.txt <<'EOF'
refactor(gz): build the gz surface as AST instead of reparsing it

The `gz*` stream family and the four zlib string functions were injected as PHP TEXT — 180 lines
tokenized and parsed on every compile that touched them. That is the one thing the "stop parsing
PHP on its own behalf" campaign removed everywhere else, and this surface landed after it, so it
was a regression against a property the tree had already reached.

TRANSCRIBED, not rewritten. `synthetic_class::transcribe_split` generated the builder calls from
the parse of the PHP, which is what makes the conversion structurally faithful rather than a
careful retyping: the emitted code IS the AST, so it cannot drift from what the parser produced,
and the transcriber PANICS on a node it cannot express rather than dropping it — a declaration
cannot go missing in the conversion.

The PHP stays, under `#[cfg(test)]`, as the migration oracle's reference. Deleting it would leave
the builder with nothing to be checked against, and the comparison is the entire reason the
conversion can be trusted: `ELEPHC_ORACLE_WHICH=gz` builds the declarations and compares them
against the parse of that PHP node by node, spans stripped. All 21 declarations match.

Verified: the oracle passes, the 28 `gz_streams` / `zlib_string_functions` / `compress_wrapper`
behaviour tests pass, and `cargo test -p elephc --lib` is 1 528 green.

The import list is derived from the transcription rather than copied from a sibling prelude, so
neither an unused import nor a missing one hides whether the conversion itself is right.

Still parsed at compile time, and not this commit's subject: `scanf_prelude` (the next one, and
also this branch's), `dir_prelude`, and `mysqli_prelude` — the last being the exception upstream
documents.
EOF
